phrases.latin: ēlixat ōllīs et cacabīs in focō
phrases.english: he boils in pots and pans on the hearth

caccabus.html: Why caccabus, not cācabus: the word is Greek κάκκαβος, with a short α and a double κ. Varro writes caccabum (Lewis & Short), and Statius scans albōrum calicum atque caccabōrum (Silv. 4.9.45) with a heavy first syllable, which the double c explains. Lewis & Short prints cācabus, marking that heavy syllable as a long vowel. Comenius’s cacabīs is marked to match.
